_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.576919/scoreboard;week=15?format=json
REDACTION: all identifiers invented — team keys, team names, manager GUIDs
(FAKEGUID...) and the recap URLs are fake. No token, email or real GUID
appears anywhere in this directory.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED: two matchups that are deliberately NOT
interchangeable, because each carries a value that breaks naive parsing:
MATCHUP A — a PLAYOFF game (is_playoffs "1") with a decided winner, both
matchup_grades, win_probability, and a recap URL containing '&'. Yahoo
HTML-escapes ampersands inside JSON string values, an artifact of the
XML→JSON transform. Stored raw, every recap link is broken; parse_scoreboard()
unescapes it back to '&'. Note that the escape appears in the URL only —
not in the recap TITLE — so a blanket unescape of every string field would
be wrong too.
MATCHUP B — a TIE. is_tied is 1 and winner_team_key is ABSENT ENTIRELY,
not empty and not one of the two teams. Both sides show identical points.
Code that reads winner_team_key without checking is_tied invents a winner
or crashes; code that treats a missing winner as 'not yet played' loses a
real result. A tie is the one outcome that has no winner and still counts.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. ⚠️ THE NUMERIC SUB-RESOURCE WRAPPER, TWICE, NESTED. 'scoreboard' is an
object whose matchups collection hangs off the key "0" while its scalar
'week' sits at the top level; and each 'matchup' repeats the pattern,
with its teams collection under ITS OWN "0" key:
league[1].scoreboard["0"].matchups["0"].matchup["0"].teams
This is the shape published wrappers index into — yfpy's data key list
for a week's scoreboard is literally ["league","scoreboard","0",
"matchups"]. See the KNOWN DISAGREEMENT note at the end.
2. matchup_grades is a list of {"matchup_grade": {team_key, grade}} and is
present on matchup A only — a grade is not always issued, and absent
grades must stay NULL rather than becoming ''.
3. team_points / team_projected_points are sub-objects with a 'total'
STRING, not numbers on the team.
4. win_probability arrives as a bare FLOAT (0.62) while every point total
is a string — inconsistent types inside one node.
5. The two sides of a matchup are stored in whatever order Yahoo emits;
parse_scoreboard() sorts by team_key so the same game ingested from the
scoreboard and from a team's own matchups endpoint canonicalizes to ONE
row instead of two. Matchup A is deliberately emitted with the
higher-numbered team FIRST so that sort is exercised.
6. 'status' is 'postevent' — Yahoo's own vocabulary, passed through
verbatim rather than normalized to something tidier.
TRUNCATED: 2 matchups of the league's 6 per week, and the team resources
carry only the fields a scoreboard actually needs. Reason: the remaining
matchups are identical code paths, and the two kept here are the only two
that differ in kind.
⚠️ KNOWN DISAGREEMENT WITH THE SHIPPED PARSER, 2026-08-11. Against parse.py
at PARSER_VERSION 1.0.0 this file parses to 0 matchups and 0 team-week
scores, SILENTLY — no exception — because flatten_resource() does not descend
into the numeric-key members of an OBJECT resource, so get(scoreboard,
"matchups") is MISSING (the scoreboard's keys are ['0','week']). Reported to
the parser author rather than papered over: removing the "0" wrappers would
make the fixture green and leave the pipeline wrong against the real API.
EXPECTED ONCE THE PARSER HANDLES THE WRAPPER (measured by hoisting the two
"0" levels in a harness, with parse.py untouched):
fantasy_matchups  2      fantasy_team_week_scores  4
side A) is_playoffs 1, is_tied 0, winner t.4, grades ('B+','A'),
recap_url unescaped to '...?week=15&mid1=4&mid2=11'
winner_team_key None, grades (None, None), recap_url None
Those are the numbers to assert.

matchup.matchup_recap_title: Third Down Thunder & Two Minute Warning: the semifinal
